statement: The landed `enforcer-lang-*` family registries are NOT uniform: enforcer-lang-ts/-security/-iac/-k8s expose `rules::registry::build_all() -> Result<Vec<RegistryRow>, DecodeError>` (RegistryRow { rule_id: &'static str, validator: Box<dyn Validator> }); enforcer-lang-common exposes a bare `registry::all(port_scope: DeclaredScope) -> Vec<Box<dyn Validator>>` (no Result, needs a DeclaredScope arg); enforcer-lang-py exposes `all_validators() -> Result<Vec<Box<dyn Validator>>, DecodeError>` (no RegistryRow wrapper); enforcer-lang-rust has landed NO aggregate registry at all yet -- only two concrete validator structs (NoReexportsValidator::new(), ErrorHandlingValidator::new(), both fallible constructors) referenced directly via their modules.
why: A router/engine that assumes one uniform 'call registry::all()' shape across every family will not compile against the real landed crates as of arc-15's HEAD (1f9ce96). This heterogeneity is exactly why the workpack scopes f05 (deep router adapters) to sibling feature packs -- the skeleton has to hand-wire each family's actual shape rather than iterate a trait-uniform list.
howToApply: When wiring `enforcer-scan`'s engine to a family crate, always Read that crate's actual `lib.rs`/`registry.rs` (or lack thereof) first -- do not assume the `build_all()->Result<Vec<RegistryRow>>` shape generalizes. When enforcer-lang-rust later lands its own aggregate (matching the `enforcer-lang-py::all_validators()` shape per that crate's own doc comment: 'enforcer-scan (arc-14/f05) dispatches by RuleId, not by vec position'), the engine.rs rust wiring collapses from two hand-listed `Box::new(...)` calls to one function call -- update `build_family_validators` in crates/enforcer-scan/src/engine.rs at that point.

statement: A `Box<dyn Validator>` returned by a family registry cannot be safely stored in a struct that must be `Sync` (required for a `rayon::par_iter` closure to capture it by reference) without `unsafe` -- `enforcer_validator::validator::Validator` has no `Send`/`Sync` supertrait bound, and Rust's auto-trait rules for trait objects are fixed at the unsizing coercion site, not inferred later from the concrete type's actual thread-safety. Since `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is a workspace-wide lint (crates/../Cargo.toml [workspace.lints.rust]), there is no safe way to reinterpret an already-erased `Box<dyn Validator>` as `Box<dyn Validator + Send + Sync>`.
why: My first engine.rs draft tried to parallelize the classify+validate dispatch itself via `par_iter` capturing `&FamilyValidators`, which only compiles if `FamilyValidators: Sync`. It is not, and cannot be made so without either (a) unsafe (forbidden) or (b) every family registry changing its return type to `Box<dyn Validator + Send + Sync>` (a breaking change to 4+ landed sibling crates arc-15 does not own).
howToApply: Split the rayon fan-out at the I/O boundary instead: parallelize file reads (`par_iter` over `&[RelPath]` producing `(RelPath, Option<String>)` pairs -- no validator trait objects cross the thread boundary), then run classify+validate sequentially over the already-collected, order-preserved results. This still delivers a genuine CPU/IO-bound rayon fan-out on the actual bottleneck (disk I/O across a large tree) and keeps the idempotency guarantee trivial (sequential fold is inherently deterministic). If a future pack needs the validator dispatch itself parallelized, it must first get every family registry to return `Box<dyn Validator + Send + Sync>` (a coordinated breaking change across arc-06/07/08/09/10/11/12), not attempt a local workaround in enforcer-scan.

evidence.ref: rustc E0277 reproduction: `dyn Foo` cannot be shared between threads safely / required for std::ptr::Unique<dyn Foo> to implement Sync -- confirmed empirically before restructuring crates/enforcer-scan/src/engine.rs's `run` function

statement: The workspace's `expect_used`/`unwrap_used` clippy lints (`[workspace.lints.clippy]` deny) apply to `#[cfg(test)]` code too -- there is no blanket test-code exemption anywhere in this workspace's lint config. Every test helper that does `"literal".parse().expect("...")` fails `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, not just production code.
why: Several other landed crates' test modules use `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` returning tests with `?` specifically because of this -- it is the established workspace idiom, not an arc-15-specific choice. My first draft of scope.rs/router/mod.rs/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs test helpers used `.expect(...)` (readable, but 12 clippy errors) before I switched every test helper to a `Result`-returning function propagated via `?` at the call site.
howToApply: When writing test fixtures/helpers in this workspace that parse a branded newtype (RuleId/RelPath/RepoRoot/etc.) from a string literal, ALWAYS make the helper return `Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (or the crate's own error type) and use `?`, never `.parse().expect(...)` or `.unwrap()`, even in `#[cfg(test)]` modules. `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (note `--all-targets`, which includes test targets) is the exact command that catches this before it becomes a proof-gate surprise.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-scan --all-targets -- -D warnings: 12 expect_used errors across router/mod.rs, rules/baseline_ratchet.rs, scope.rs test modules, all resolved by converting helpers to Result-returning + ? propagation; 0 errors after

statement: A live read-only self-scan of this workspace's own crates/ tree (1173 files walked, ok=false, 2068 violations + 20 warnings = 2088 total findings across ~140+ distinct RuleIds) confirms the arc-15 engine end-to-end: walk -> classify -> route -> validate -> fold all function correctly against real, non-fixture code. Notable: a large share of the raw finding count is expected noise, not real defects -- TS-5.1/TS-5.2/TS-7.12/TS-7.13 (each ~140 hits) are the TS generic-scanner slice firing on this Rust-only workspace's non-existent TS toolchain config (expected: no tsconfig/eslint config exists here, so 'config missing/misconfigured' rules fire universally), and several ARCH-1.x/AI-1.x hits point directly at crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/families/*/fixtures/*/fail.txt files -- i.e. the engine correctly found the family crate's OWN seeded fail-fixtures, which are supposed to trip, not genuine self-violations.
why: This is the strongest available proof the workpack calls for (a live self-scan of the workspace that built the engine), but the raw violation count is misleading read in isolation -- a future pack building on this engine (e.g. a real `enforcer scan --self` CI gate, or the d02 baseline-ratchet's first real baseline) needs to exclude `tests/fixtures/**` and family crates' own `fixtures/**` dirs (or apply the baseline-ratchet) before the count means anything as a health signal, and needs a real project config (arc-03 EffectiveConfig) wired through `enforcer-scan::walk::IgnoreRules` before TS-family rules stop firing wall-to-wall on a workspace with no TS toolchain.
howToApply: When any future pack (arc-16 coordination CI gate, a10 self-enforcement, arc-17 proof) runs `enforcer-scan` against this workspace for real, thread `EffectiveConfig.ignore_dirs`/`ignore_file_globs` through `IgnoreRules` (not `IgnoreRules::default()`) and exclude `**/fixtures/**` at minimum, or seed a d02 baseline from this first scan so only NEW violations from that point block.

evidence.ref: cargo run -p enforcer-scan --example self_scan (scratch, not committed) against workspace root at HEAD 1f9ce96: walked 1173 files, ok=false, violations=2068, warnings=20; top offenders TS-5.1/TS-5.2/TS-7.12/TS-7.13 each 140 hits; several ARCH-1.x/AI-1.x hits point at crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/families/*/fixtures/*/fail.txt

statement: arc-15-enforcer-scan.md's own body (Requirement Checklist + Where We Want To Be) directs arc-15 to implement `src/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs` as d02's 'full behavioral contract,' but WORKPACK_INDEX.md's arc-15 row and d02-baseline-grandfather-ratchet.md both say d02 (deps: arc-15, d01-rule-mechanization-engine) owns that exact file + tests/fixtures/baseline_ratchet/** and specifies a materially larger deliverable: a Validator impl over the aggregated Report, a versioned serde baseline record with a Sha256 integrity hash persisted via enforcer-core's append utilities, and an `enforcer check --baseline write` CLI mode. I followed the workpack's literal instruction (per protocol step: 'execute workpack exactly') and landed an in-memory ratchet()/Baseline/BaselineKey core (fail-closed on new, ratchet-down on fixed, tested with 4 unit tests) as a reusable primitive -- NOT a Validator, no persistence, no Sha256, no CLI mode. This is real but partial coverage of d02's stated deliverable.
why: The workpack body and the index/sibling-workpack disagree on scope (same tension pattern as mem-arc-13-0001, but this time the workpack BODY over-claims into a sibling's territory rather than the index being silent). A future d02 executor must not assume 'arc-15 already did this' from a DONE/GREEN status on arc-15's row -- the persistence/Validator/CLI layers are still fully open.
howToApply: When d02 is assigned: read this crate's crates/enforcer-scan/src/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs module doc comment first (it documents this exact conflict inline) before deciding what remains. Build the Validator/serde-record/Sha256/CLI layer ON TOP of the existing ratchet()/Baseline/BaselineKey pure functions (they are a legitimate reusable core, not scaffolding to discard) rather than rewriting them. Add tests/fixtures/baseline_ratchet/** as d02's own owned directory (arc-15 did not create it).

evidence.ref: docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/arc-15-enforcer-scan.md line 25 & Requirement Checklist vs WORKPACK_INDEX.md line 52 ('hosts d02 (d02 owns src/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs+fixtures; arc-15 skeleton only)') and line 110, vs docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/d02-baseline-grandfather-ratchet.md full Requirement Checklist (Validator impl, Sha256 baseline record, --baseline CLI mode -- none implemented by arc-15)
